\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Polynomial}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Polynomial
\section{Overview}
Independent affine decomposition gives second- and fourth-moment identities for multilinear evaluations. Vanishing odd input moments and bounded fourth-to-second moment ratios imply the degree-dependent generalized Bonami bound.

\difficulty{6}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,X\in L^4(\mu)$ be real-valued
functions. Suppose $X$ is independent of the pair $(A,D)$ and
$\mathbb{E}X=\mathbb{E}X^3=0$. Then
$\mathbb{E}(A+XD)^2=\mathbb{E}A^2+\mathbb{E}X^2\,\mathbb{E}D^2$ and
$\mathbb{E}(A+XD)^4=\mathbb{E}A^4+6\,\mathbb{E}X^2\,\mathbb{E}(A^2D^2)+\mathbb{E}X^4\,\mathbb{E}D^4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cauchy–Schwarz for Fourth Moments]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.cauchy_schwarz}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measure space, and let $A,D\in L^4(\mu)$ be real-valued
functions. Then $\left(\int A^2D^2\,d\mu\right)^2\leq\left(\int
A^4\,d\mu\right)\left(\int D^4\,d\mu\right)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Independence from Sums Omitting a Coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.indep_sum_of_notMem}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $n$ be a natural number, and let
$X_j:\Omega\to\bbr$ for $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be mutually independent and almost
everywhere measurable. Let $F$ and $G$ be real coefficient families on subsets of the
coordinate set, let $s$ be a subset of that set, and let $i$ be a coordinate with
$i\notin s$. Then $X_i$ is independent of the pair consisting of $\sum_{T\subseteq
s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j$ and $\sum_{T\subseteq s}G(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{7}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a real
coefficient family indexed by subsets of $[n]$ that vanishes on every set of size
greater than $k$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables on
this space, each with finite fourth moment, mean zero, and third moment zero. Suppose
$B\ge1$ and each $X_i$ is $B$-reasonable, meaning its fourth moment is at most $B$ times
the square of its second moment. Then $F(X)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$
has finite fourth moment and is $\max(B,9)^k$-reasonable.
\end{theorem}
